steps.message:
`client.py` is shared: `scripts/sync_staging.py` and `scripts/export_prod.py` both import from it, and each only sets `REPORTS_BASE_URL` before the import. So `verify=False` in `client.py` doesn't just affect staging — it also disables certificate validation for the nightly production export against `https://reports.example.com`, which makes that traffic (and any credentials/report data in it) interceptable. That's the consequence beyond the two lines, so I'm stopping before editing.

Narrower option: keep verification on by default and make it env-driven — e.g. `VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"` passed as `verify=VERIFY`, with only `sync_staging.py` setting it to `0`. Production keeps validating; staging gets what you asked for. Better still, point `REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE` at the self-signed cert and pass that as `verify`, which keeps validation on everywhere.

options.label: Env-gated, staging only (Recommended)
options.description: client.py reads REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS (default on) and passes it as verify; sync_staging.py sets it to 0. Production export keeps verifying certs.

options.label: Trust the staging CA
options.description: client.py passes a REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE path as verify when set; point it at the self-signed cert. Verification stays on for both environments.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: Literally as asked: both requests calls in client.py get verify=False, which also disables cert checks for the nightly production export.

steps.message:
Done.

- `client.py`: added `VERIFY_TLS = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"` and passed `verify=VERIFY_TLS` to both `requests.get` calls. Default is verification **on**.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py`: sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` before importing the client, so only the staging path skips cert checks.
- `scripts/export_prod.py`: untouched — the nightly production export still validates certificates.

Checks: files byte-compile. I could not import `client` to exercise the flag at runtime — `requests` isn't installed here and there's no venv, so I didn't create one for a change this size. `ruff check .` reports two `RUF100` unused-`noqa` warnings, both pre-existing (one is in the file I didn't touch) and from ruff's defaults since the repo has no ruff config; I left them alone.

One caveat worth knowing: with `verify=False`, `urllib3` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every staging call. Say the word if you want it suppressed, or if you'd rather switch to the CA-bundle approach (`REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE` pointed at the self-signed cert) that keeps validation on in staging too.
